title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-21

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard captures a stellar ’73 performance highlighted by the legendary Playin’ > El Paso > Wharf Rat > Morning Dew jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine sound‑board capture with excellent separation and clarity (aside from a minor pitch‑shift quirk and occasional splice), making every nuance of the band audible. Musically the show shines – the first set grooves strong, but the second‑set “Playin’ > El Paso > Playin’ > Wharf Rat > Playin’ > Morning Dew” marathon is repeatedly called one of the all‑time great Dead jams, and songs like Here Comes Sunshine, Half Step, Big River and Weather Report Suite add to the magic. While a few reviewers note occasional tuning slips, the consensus is that this night ranks among the very best of 1973.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈ 4.7/5 across 24 reviews, with overwhelming praise for both performance and sound quality; only minor criticisms (tuning slips, pitch shift) temper an otherwise stellar assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with great instrument separation; a few listeners mention a slight high‑pitch anomaly and occasional splice/level adjustments, but overall the sound is clean and very listenable.

standout_songs: Playin' In The Band > El Paso > Playin' > Wharf Rat > Playin' > Morning Dew
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds momentum with tight, energetic numbers; the second set features seamless segues and a monumental jam sandwich that many reviewers cite as a career‑high moment.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is described as exploratory, inventive (especially on Jack Straw and the jam sequence) and unusually forward in the mix; a few note missed notes/tuning slips but overall his playing is praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh delivers solid bass foundation with occasional “fuzzy‑fat” tones noted during Half Step; generally regarded as reliable and supportive.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work shines, highlighted by a duet with Lesh on Looks Like Rain and near‑solo moments on Big River; his vocals are praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (keys) receives strong commendation for crisp breaks, great solos, and overall keyboard texture that adds depth to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is highlighted as a “snap” on Big River and driving throughout the jam sections, contributing to the tight‑loose feel.
